extracted.intended_audience: corporate PR teams and PR agencies producing international press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and standards for localizing and distributing corporate press releases across global markets, covering translation vs localization, cultural adaptation, required localized elements, regulatory compliance, timing, and distribution channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation (literal language conversion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Literal language conversion that closely matches the source language and does not address cultural nuances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when fidelity to the original wording is required, but be aware that translation alone often fails to account for tone, cultural references, or local expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization (adjust for cultural relevance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adapts language, tone, references, audience expectations, local data, market insights, and regulatory considerations so the release resonates in the target market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize intent and impact over literal translation; localization can include changing examples, idioms, imagery, and references to align with local norms and consumer behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic approach: structure first, then localized translations
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a clear structure for the release before creating localized translations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the core structure and intent are agreed upon centrally; then local teams adapt language and examples so the message reads naturally and achieves the intended impact in-market.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global consistency + local flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Key messaging must be evident and the same in all markets while allowing flexibility for tailored, locally effective content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain core messages/claims across markets but permit local adaptations in tone, examples, imagery, and supporting materials to optimize resonance and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain key messaging consistency across markets
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the central, brand-level messages are evident and consistent in every localized version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local changes should not alter core claims, positioning, or legal disclosures; use back-translation or central reviews to confirm consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow local flexibility and adjust approach to what works locally
rubrics_metrics.description: Permit local teams to tailor wording, tone, and examples according to what performs best in their market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document acceptable ranges of adaptation and approval workflows so local creativity stays aligned with brand and legal requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural adaptation — holidays and calendar considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Account for local holidays, festivals, and market-specific calendar events when scheduling and framing campaigns (e.g., Black Friday vs Singles Day).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid scheduling around local religious festivals or bank holidays; use local equivalents (e.g., Singles Day in China) and coordinate timing with time zones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural sensitivities — symbols, imagery, and conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure color symbolism, number meanings, imagery (food, gestures), names/naming conventions, and hierarchy in quotes are culturally appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review visuals and language for local taboos and interpretive differences; consider local naming order, honorifics, and whether certain imagery is offensive or misunderstood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution and timing tailored to local news cycles
rubrics_metrics.description: Schedule distribution according to local news cycles, deadlines, and time zones rather than central office hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with local media calendars, avoid local holidays, and adapt to different newsroom deadlines to maximize pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic localization elements (headline, body, formats)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include translated headline and body plus localized formats such as local currency conversion, local units (metric/imperial), local date format, and phone number formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardize the set of localized elements required for each market and validate formatting conventions (e.g., DD/MM vs MM/DD) with local reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural adaptation elements (local quotes, case studies, statistics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include quotes from local executives, local case studies, local statistics, and references to local context to increase relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer local spokespeople and evidence where possible; these elements boost credibility and media interest in-market.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory compliance per market
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the release complies with market-specific regulations such as GDPR (EU), privacy laws, industry-specific regulations, disclosure requirements, and language laws (e.g., French in Quebec).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult legal/compliance teams for each jurisdiction; adapt disclosures, data handling language, and mandatory statements to local law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local PR contact
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a local PR/contact person for media inquiries in each market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include local phone numbers, email addresses, time zone availability, and response expectations; this helps journalists and supports timely follow-ups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Native speaker review
rubrics_metrics.description: Have localized content reviewed by a native speaker of the target language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use native-speaking communications professionals (not only translators) to check tone, idiom, and appropriateness; native review reduces risk of awkward phrasing or offense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation back to source language reviewed
rubrics_metrics.description: Review a back-translation to the source language to verify that localized versions preserve intent and meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use back-translation as a quality control step to detect meaning drift and ensure brand/legal claims remain intact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brand voice maintained
rubrics_metrics.description: Preserve the brand's voice and personality across localized releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document brand tone guidelines and provide examples to localizers; reconcile local naturalness with brand consistency during reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid culturally insensitive imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure visuals are not offensive or insensitive in the target market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Screen images for local taboos (gestures, food, dress, religious symbols) and replace or adapt imagery as necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local market-specific data
rubrics_metrics.description: Include data and statistics specific to the local market to enhance relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Source local research or metrics where possible; avoid relying solely on global figures unless clearly labeled as such.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local competitive context
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference or be aware of the local competitive landscape when positioning claims or comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid statements that may be misleading in a local context; tailor competitive references to what is true and meaningful in-market.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinated across markets
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate messaging, timing, and distribution across markets to manage global rollouts and avoid contradictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish central-local workflows, timing plans, and approval gates so launches are synchronized and consistent where intended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of local distribution channels and partners
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage local wire services, regional PR agency partners, and native-language journalist databases for distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build relationships with local partners and maintain multi-language press kits to increase reach and credibility in each market.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-language press kit
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a press kit with materials in multiple languages for journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include localized assets (images with localized captions, localized fact sheets, and bios) to simplify reporting and encourage accurate coverage.
